title: Coefficient compatibility square for the actual projection mate
statement:
In the standing separated finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism and $a:R\to S$ a map of commutative condensed rings such that scalar extension is exact on every scheme. In the ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories put $T_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$, $P_R=Lf_R^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$, and similarly for $S$. Let $c_f:T_XP_R\cong P_ST_Y$ and $\gamma_f:T_YG_R\to G_ST_X$ be the specified comparisons [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso, def-sfb-derived-push-hom]. Let $\mu_Z:T_Z(A\otimes_R^LB)\cong T_ZA\otimes_S^LT_ZB$ be the canonical scalar tensor comparison. For $K\in D(R_X),M\in D(R_Y)$ put $H=K\otimes_R^LP_RM$, and let $\pi^R,\pi^S$ be the projection morphisms [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Then, with rightmost map applied first,
$$\pi^S_{T_XK,T_YM}\circ(\gamma_{f,K}\otimes1)\circ\mu_Y
=G_S((1\otimes c_{f,M})\circ\mu_X)\circ\gamma_{f,H}\circ T_Y(\pi^R_{K,M}).$$
Both sides run from $T_Y(G_RK\otimes_R^LM)$ to $G_S(T_XK\otimes_S^LP_ST_YM)$. No properness, constructibility, or invertibility of a projection or push comparison is assumed.

proof.text: Use the section-ring equivalences of [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] for both coefficients $R$ and $S$. They identify the actual module-object tensors, derived pullbacks $P_R,P_S$, pushforwards $G_R,G_S$, the derived adjunctions $P\dashv G$ with their counits, and the pullback tensor maps $d^R,d^S$ with the canonical ringed-topos ones. That theorem fixes one coefficient ring; the coefficient change is transported separately by [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction], applied on $Z=X,Y$ to the ring-object map $a_Z:R_Z\to S_Z$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]: it identifies internal $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$, $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z}$, the K-flat derived extension $T_Z$, the exact derived restriction $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z})$ and the specified derived adjunction $T_Z\dashv D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z})$, including unit and counit, with the sectionwise ones. Thus $T_Z$ is $L\phi_Z^*$ for the ringed-topos morphism $\phi_Z:(Z,S_Z)\to(Z,R_Z)$ with identity underlying topos, and $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z})$ is $R\phi_{Z*}$: restriction is exact and, since $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$ preserves finite limits, sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives], so on a K-injective complex both are restriction termwise. The coefficient squares in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] make the two composites $(X,S_X)\to(Y,R_Y)$ equal as ringed-topos morphisms: same underlying morphism $f$, and ring maps $\alpha'_f\circ f^*a_Y=a_X\circ\alpha_f$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] to this square with identity commutation, path $1$ being $\phi_X$ after $f_R$ (so $P_1=T_XP_R$, $V_1=G_RD(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$) and path $2$ being $f_S$ after $\phi_Y$ (so $P_2=P_ST_Y$, $V_2=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})G_S$). Its direct-image comparison $V_1\cong V_2$ is $e^{-1}$, where $e:D(\mathrm{Res}_{a_Y})G_S\cong G_RD(\mathrm{Res}_{a_X})$ is [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso]. Indeed, compute both on a K-injective complex $I$ of $S_X$-modules. By the normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], $\kappa_{f_R,\phi_X}$ at $I$ is the identity class of $f_*\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}I$ (one may take the resolution $j=\mathrm{id}$, as $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}I$ is K-injective), and $\kappa_{\phi_Y,f_S}$ at $I$ is the class of $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}f_*I$ (restriction being exact, $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}(j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and represents the identification of $R\phi_{Y*}$ with $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})$). The ordinary commutation between them is the underived isomorphism $\theta_I$ of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso], an identity of module sheaves since both sides are $f_*$ followed by restriction along $\eta'_f\circ a_Y=f_*a_X\circ\eta_f$. The component of $e$ at $QI$ in the definition [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso] is $Q(\theta_I)$ between the same representatives. Both are natural in the derived argument, so they agree. Consequently the lemma's pullback comparison $\theta:P_2\cong P_1$, whose conjugate is $e^{-1}$, equals $\sigma:=c^{-1}$ where $c$ is the conjugate of $e$ specified in [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso], rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of these functors. All sites are taken small in the module-sheaf universe as in the cited section-ring equivalence. Exact scalar extension supplies the flatness hypothesis in the specified definition of $e$; the cited ringed-topos lemma needs no flatness.

proof.text:
Write $\sigma=c^{-1}$ and let $d^R,d^S$ denote the pullback tensor comparisons in [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. The tensor equation of [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction], applied to the same square and transported by [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison], reads, for $A,B\in D(R_Y)$,
$$
(\sigma_A\otimes\sigma_B)d^S_{T_YA,T_YB}P_S(\mu_{Y;A,B})
=\mu_{X;P_RA,P_RB}T_X(d^R_{A,B})\sigma_{A\otimes B}.\tag{1}
$$
Indeed the tensor comparison for the composite $P_ST_Y$ is $d^S P_S(\mu_Y)$, while for $T_XP_R$ it is $\mu_XT_X(d^R)$. The scalar tensor comparisons here are the ringed-topos tensor maps $t_{\phi_Z}$ of the identity-topos coefficient morphisms. They are the canonical $\mu_Z$ of the statement, in the same direction: on flat-term K-flat representatives both are the localization of the termwise map $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ on local pure tensors, and the transports of Step 1 [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] preserve local pure tensors and these representatives.

proof.text:
The definitions [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso, def-sfb-derived-push-hom, def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso, def-sfb-mate-push-hom] give the following counit equation:
$$\varepsilon^S_{T_XK}P_S(\gamma_K)=T_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\sigma_{G_RK}.\tag{2}$$
Here is the calculation, including the relation between the two different mates. Put $U=D(\mathrm{Res}_{a_X})$, $V=D(\mathrm{Res}_{a_Y})$, and write $\eta^X,v^X,v^Y$ for the scalar unit on $X$ and scalar counits on $X,Y$. The mate definition says $\gamma_K=v^Y_{G_ST_XK}T_Y(e^{-1}_{T_XK})T_YG_R(\eta^X_K)$. Conjugacy for the composite adjunctions, whose counits are those of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], says
$$\varepsilon^S_B P_S(v^Y_{G_SB})P_ST_Y(e^{-1}_B)=v^X_BT_X(\varepsilon^R_{UB})\sigma_{G_RUB}.$$
Substitute $B=T_XK$ and precompose with $P_ST_YG_R(\eta^X_K)$. Naturality of $\sigma$ moves this last map to $T_XP_RG_R(\eta^X_K)$; naturality of $\varepsilon^R$ turns $\varepsilon^R_{UT_XK}P_RG_R(\eta^X_K)$ into $\eta^X_K\varepsilon^R_K$. Finally $v^X_{T_XK}T_X(\eta^X_K)=1$ is the scalar adjunction triangle. This proves (2).

Set $A=G_RK\otimes_R^LM$, $H=K\otimes_R^LP_RM$, $B=T_XK\otimes_S^LP_ST_YM$, and $q=(1\otimes c_M)\mu_{X;K,P_RM}:T_XH\to B$. To compare the two maps $T_YA\to G_SB$, apply the injective adjunction bijection of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]: the transpose of $h$ is $\varepsilon^S_B P_S(h)$. By the defining transpose of $\pi^S$ in [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map] and naturality of $d^S$, the transpose of the left side of the claimed equation is
$$(\varepsilon^S_{T_XK}P_S\gamma_K\otimes1)d^S_{T_YG_RK,T_YM}P_S\mu_Y.$$
Use (2), insert $c_M\sigma_M=1$, and use (1) at $(G_RK,M)$. This becomes
$$(T_X\varepsilon^R_K\otimes c_M)\mu_{X;P_RG_RK,P_RM}T_X(d^R_{G_RK,M})\sigma_A
=q\,T_X((\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1)d^R_{G_RK,M})\sigma_A,\tag{3}$$
where the last equality is naturality of $\mu_X$ in the first variable.

source.place: paragraph (3): transpose and calculate the left-hand projection composite

proof.text:
For the right side $G_S(q)\gamma_HT_Y(\pi^R_{K,M})$, naturality of $\varepsilon^S$ followed by (2) at $H$ gives transpose
$$q\,T_X(\varepsilon^R_H)\sigma_{G_RH}P_ST_Y(\pi^R_{K,M}).$$
Naturality of $\sigma$ makes this
$$q\,T_X(\varepsilon^R_HP_R(\pi^R_{K,M}))\sigma_A
=q\,T_X((\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1)d^R_{G_RK,M})\sigma_A.$$
The last equality is precisely the defining transpose of $\pi^R$ in [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. This is (3). The adjunction bijection in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] therefore gives the required equality of the original maps. No cancellation of $\gamma$ or of a projection morphism occurred, so no invertibility or properness hypothesis is needed.
